extracted.intended_audience: clinicians and authors preparing medical case reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reporting individual patient case reports for publication, specifying required sections and the information each should contain. Focused on completeness, transparency, and reproducibility of clinical case reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagnosis or intervention of primary focus followed by the words “case report”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep title specific about the primary diagnosis or intervention and explicitly label the article as a 'case report' to aid indexing and reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Words
rubrics_metrics.description: 2 to 5 key words that identify diagnoses or interventions in this case report (including "case report").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 2–5 concise terms that reflect the main clinical issues or interventions; include 'case report' as one keyword.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract (structured or unstructured)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract should include: Introduction – What is unique about this case and what does it add to the scientific literature? The patient’s main concerns and important clinical findings. The primary diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes. Conclusion – What are one or more 'take-away' lessons from this case report?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be written in a structured or unstructured format but should cover these four elements so readers quickly grasp uniqueness, presentation, management, and lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction (body)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarizes why this case is unique and may include medical literature references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set context and justify publication by explaining novelty, educational value, or gap in the literature; cite relevant prior reports or literature where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Information
rubrics_metrics.description: De-identified patient specific information. Primary concerns and symptoms of the patient. Medical, family, and psychosocial history including relevant genetic information. Relevant past interventions and their outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient de-identified background to understand comorbidities, risk factors, and prior treatments; include social/family/genetic details when relevant to the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe significant physical examination (PE) and important clinical findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report objective signs and notable exam results that informed diagnosis or management decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical and current information from this episode of care organized as a timeline (figure or table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present events chronologically, ideally as a figure or table, to clarify sequence of symptoms, investigations, interventions, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic methods (PE, laboratory testing, imaging, surveys). Diagnostic challenges. Diagnosis (including other diagnoses considered). Prognostic characteristics when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the tests and methods used, differential diagnoses considered, obstacles or uncertainties in reaching a diagnosis, and any prognosis-related features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic Intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of therapeutic intervention (pharmacologic, surgical, preventive). Administration of therapeutic intervention (dosage, strength, duration). Changes in therapeutic interventions with explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify intervention details (drug names, doses, schedules, operative details), rationale for choices, and any subsequent modifications and their reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinician- and patient-assessed outcomes if available. Important follow-up diagnostic and other test results. Intervention adherence and tolerability. (How was this assessed?) Adverse and unanticipated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both objective and subjective outcome measures, subsequent test findings, how adherence/tolerability were evaluated, and any complications or unexpected events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengths and limitations in your approach to this case. Discussion of the relevant medical literature. The rationale for your conclusions. The primary 'take-away' lessons from this case report (without references) in a one paragraph conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically appraise the case, compare it to existing literature, explain reasoning behind conclusions, acknowledge limitations, and provide a concise take-away paragraph (no citations) summarizing practical lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: The patient should share their perspective on the treatment(s) they received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short first-person account from the patient describing their experience, preferences, or perceived outcomes when possible and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The patient should give informed consent. (Provide if requested.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and document the patient's informed consent for publication; be prepared to provide evidence of consent to editors or publishers upon request.
